WHY: Every spec-compliant browser report fails validation on the missing destination/attempts, so the endpoint returns 422 for the whole batch and processes no reports, leaving the collector functionally dead. HOW: Mark both fields optional (required=False) or drop them from the serializer.

The humanized schedule_type is written to a config copy that is never returned, so the occurrence's monitor context still contains the raw numeric schedule_type. — WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context humanizes schedule_type on a throwaway copy of monitor.config but returns the original monitor.config, so the humanization never reaches the output. WHY: the monitor context sent to the issue platform in event_data (line 89) always carries the raw numeric schedule_type enum value instead of the intended display string, and the dead `config` copy misleads future maintenance. HOW: return the mutated copy ("config": config) or, if the raw config is intentional, delete the copy/mutation lines — note this defect was carried over verbatim from the old mark_failed.py; the PR relocated it rather than introduced it.

The retryCount update inside the catch block is itself unguarded, so a failed update escapes the loop and aborts the whole SMS cron run. — WHAT: The catch block added at line 190 performs an unguarded `await prisma.workflowReminder.update`, so any failure of this update (e.g. Prisma P2025 when the reminder row was deleted mid-run by a booking cascade or an overlapping cron run's deleteMany) is thrown out of the catch. WHY: The exception escapes the for-loop and the handler, so all remaining unscheduled reminders in that run are skipped and the cron endpoint returns a 500 — a failure mode that did not exist before this PR, since the catch previously only logged. HOW: Use `updateMany` (silently no-ops on missing rows) or wrap the update in its own try/catch: `await prisma.workflowReminder.updateMany({ where: { id: reminder.id }, data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } })`.

retryCount is incremented from a stale in-memory snapshot instead of atomically, allowing lost updates when cron runs overlap. — WHAT: retryCount is incremented via `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value snapshotted at findMany time, in both the else branch (line 184) and the catch block (line 195). WHY: This endpoint is a cron API; if two runs overlap (long handler with per-reminder Twilio/DB calls, or a cron-service retry), both runs read the same count and write the same result, losing an increment so a permanently failing reminder survives longer than the intended two-failure limit. HOW: Use Prisma's atomic increment: `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`.

The retryCount>1 delete branch has no method or scheduled filter, so the SMS cron can delete non-SMS reminders once any other writer adopts retryCount. — WHAT: The second OR branch of the deleteMany (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or `scheduled: false`) filter, unlike the first branch. WHY: retryCount is a column on the shared WorkflowReminder table (also used by EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders, and the WhatsApp cron shares this table); any future/non-SMS writer that adopts retryCount, or any backfilled row, would have its reminders silently deleted by the SMS cron regardless of method or scheduled state. HOW: Add the same constraints as the SMS path: `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 }`.

New helper _create_process_for_shard is dead code — no caller exists and the intended per-shard restart routing is never used. — WHAT: The newly added _create_process_for_shard (singular) has no call sites — _ensure_processes_alive always restarts via _create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards), and no other code in the diff invokes the singular helper. WHY: The per-shard restart routing it implements was never wired up, leaving dead code that misleads readers into thinking per-shard restarts exist; if it were later called it would silently do nothing for a shard not present in process_to_shards_map (no else branch). HOW: Delete the method, or wire it into _ensure_processes_alive if per-shard restart granularity was the intent.

Hang-restart of a thread-mode flusher now duplicates the flusher thread instead of crashing, which can double-produce segments since flush_segments is a peek, not a claim. — WHAT: When a flusher thread (produce_to_pipe is not None) is detected as hung, the new isinstance guard skips kill() for non-process workers but _create_process_for_shards still runs, starting a second thread while the hung one is still alive. WHY: flush_segments only peeks queue keys via ZRANGEBYSCORE and deletion is deferred to done_flush_segments after producing, so two concurrent flushers over the same shards can fetch and produce the same segments — duplicate segment production and an unkillable orphan thread; previously this path crashed the consumer instead (Thread.kill raised an uncaught AttributeError), so the duplicate-flusher state is newly reachable. HOW: For thread workers, either refuse to restart while the old thread is alive (log and skip), or track a per-shard 'owner' generation token so a stale thread stops flushing after a replacement starts.

New TotalDocs() log call races with the just-started watch-event goroutine's unlocked cache writes, causing a fatal concurrent map read/write crash. — WHAT: The new startup log line calls s.search.TotalDocs() concurrently with the event-consumption goroutine started at search.go:207-213, but bleveBackend.TotalDocs (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:198-207) iterates b.cache without acquiring cacheMu. WHY: handleEvent → getOrCreateIndex → BuildIndex writes b.cache under cacheMu (bleve.go:191-193); a concurrent unlocked map iteration triggers Go's fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' runtime error, crashing the whole process during the startup window (any write event arriving right as init finishes, e.g. in HA deployments with active writers). HOW: Take cacheMu.RLock()/RUnlock() around the map iteration in bleveBackend.TotalDocs.

Removing the whole-function cacheMu lets concurrent same-key BuildIndex calls race bleve.New on the same directory, so builds that previously succeeded can now fail. — WHAT: Removing the whole-function cacheMu from BuildIndex allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource (there is no serialization on the getOrCreateIndex→build→BuildIndex path — searchSupport has no lock; builderCache.mu at search.go:395/450-451 only guards document-builder cache misses). WHY: Both goroutines call bleve.New on the same directory Root/Namespace/Resource.Group (bleve.go:151-152); bleve.New fails when the path already exists, so concurrent first-touch builds (a Search RPC racing a watch event for a resource below InitMinCount that was never prebuilt) can now fail together, whereas the previous coarse lock guaranteed the first build completed and was cached before a second one started. HOW: Deduplicate in-flight builds per key (e.g. singleflight.Group or a per-key 'building' set guarded by cacheMu, re-checking the cache after acquiring) in BuildIndex or getOrCreateIndex.
